paper_diagnosis: Lyme disease causing culture-negative prosthetic-joint-infection mimic
presentation_summary: 83-year-old man from central Pennsylvania with a left total knee arthroplasty 6 years earlier developed 3 days of knee pain, erythema, fever, moderate effusion, and limited range of motion.
Synovial aspiration showed WBC 17,370/uL with 92% neutrophils and no crystals; cultures were negative.
Inflammatory markers were ESR 64 mm/h and CRP 6.7 mg/dL. He underwent resection arthroplasty with static antibiotic spacer because prosthetic joint infection was suspected.

Intraoperative findings included purulence and synovitis, but intraoperative cultures were negative. Serum Lyme testing was positive by screening and IgG Western blot, and synovial-fluid Borrelia PCR was positive.
He received doxycycline followed by IV ceftriaxone. Repeat synovial PCR was negative before reimplantation, and he was asymptomatic with a functional revision knee at 1 year.
